transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-10
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Kim (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Redwood SE), Olivia Martinez (Blueleaf CISO), David Braun (Blueleaf Dir Cloud Ops), Priya Singh (Blueleaf Legal), Marcus Lee (Blueleaf Platform)

Summary: security-focused review on data residency, region pinning, cross-border processing, and sub-processors. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/On-prem) tradeoffs, BYOK/KMS options, audit logs and retention, SCCs/DPA, RBAC/SSO and SCIM. Agreed to share SOC2/ISO and architecture runbook; legal review of DPA/SCCs to follow.

00:00 Samira: hey everyone, thanks for making time, I think we have about 45-50 minutes. quick round of intros?
00:08 Olivia: yeah im Olivia, CISO at Blueleaf, i'll lead security questions.
00:11 David: David, cloud ops, will be focused on region and infra implications.
00:15 Priya: Priya from legal, i'll look at DPA and SCCs.
00:18 Samira: great, quick agenda, run through residency and region pinning, sub-processors list, encryption/BYOK, audit logging and retention, and then next steps. Jonah will handle the deep infra bits.
00:31 Jonah: hi, thanks — I'll start with a quick overview of how Redwood handles region pinning and options you have. first, we have three deployment modes: hosted (multi-region), dedicated (reserved capacity pinned to region(s)), and private (VPC or on-prem). for residency the choices are: pin to a single region in AWS eu-west-1 or us-east-1, or choose Dedicated pools that we reserve in your customer-account region, or Private where control plane is customer-managed.
00:58 Marcus: when you say private, is that fully air-gapped or just VPC peering?
01:03 Jonah: good q — private can be deployed in a customer VPC with customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM integrations, if you need air-gapped on-prem we have a package but that's more involved. most regulated financials pick Private or Dedicated to meet residency.
01:22 Olivia: primary ask is EU-only processing and no cross-border export of unredacted customer data. also want to know sub-processors — do you use any US-based services that might trigger transfer?
01:31 Lina: we keep control-plane metadata in our control plane, but with Private you can host control plane inside your VPC; otherwise hosted control plane metadata may transit. sub-processors commonly used: AWS (EU regions), Google Cloud sometimes for specific customers, and a small set of telemetry vendors — we can provide the sub-processor list and their subprocess location.
01:50 Priya: on the legal side we need standard contractual clauses (SCCs) and a DPA that states no transfer outside EU unless covered by SCCs or adequacy. also need to understand retention and the ability to request deletion.
02:02 Samira: absolutely — we ship a DPA and Sccs template; we also have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certs. i'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts after the call.
02:12 David: how granular is region pinning? can we pin at a per-tenant or per-route level, or is it at account level?
02:20 Jonah: currently we support per-customer and per-deployment region pinning. hosted API allows region hints but not strict hard pinning (requests may route for latency/fallback). Dedicated is reserved in specific region(s) and Private is fully customer controlled. some customers implement a per-tenant routing policy — we can document our options. note: there is an option to pin by model or route in advanced configs but that needs Dedicated or Private to guarantee no cross-region fallback.
02:52 Marcus: what about logging and audit trails — do logs leave the region?
02:57 Lina: audit logs for Private are stored in your logging stack if you host the control plane; for Dedicated we can configure log retention within the region with limited control plane telemetry. hosted by default stores logs in our primary region but we offer log-forwarding to your SIEM in-region.
03:15 Olivia: encryption questions — at rest and in transit, and can we bring our own key (BYOK)?
03:21 Jonah: data in transit is TLS. at rest we encrypt with customer-supplied KMS if Private or we support BYOK via an integrated KMS/HSM for Dedicated customers. hosted supports customer-managed keys in certain cases; we'll include exact modes in the doc. note: for EU-only requirement BYOK + Private deployment is the strongest guarantee.
03:42 Priya: how do you handle backups and replicas — could those go outside EU?
03:47 Lina: backups for Dedicated and Private can be configured to remain in-region. hosted backups may be replicated for resilience; we have options to limit to EU but this depends on the failover policy. we'll put the backup replication policy in the runbook.
04:05 David: what's the list of sub-processors? do you share their localization and privacy docs?
04:10 Samira: yes, we'll share the current sub-processor roster (AWS eu-west-1, Azure EU regions optional, Datadog/workflow vendors — we'll annotate country locations). keep in mind some telemetry vendors may be US-based; we can offer an enterprise-only configuration that disables those.
04:30 Olivia: Schrems II implications — are you committing to SCCs? and do you have any Data Access by US government risk via sub-processors?
04:39 Priya: yes that's what I'm looking for too.
04:42 Jonah: we currently execute SCCs in our DPA. for sub-processors like AWS, they commit to EU region storage for specific ARNs. we recommend Dedicated or Private to minimize risk surface. we do not hold any decryption keys for BYOK configurations.
04:58 Marcus: if we do Dedicated in eu-west-1, and a model fallback happens (say eu capacity exhausted), will requests route to us-east?
05:06 Jonah: by default no — Dedicated has strict region affinity. hosted can fallback. if you require absolute no cross-border processing, Dedicated or Private with enforced policies is the recommendation. we'll include configuration flags in the runbook to disable cross-region fallback.
05:23 Olivia: audit logs retention — how long and can we set custom retention for compliance?
05:27 Lina: yes, retention is configurable in Dedicated and Private. hosted has default retention 90 days for token-level traces, you can pay for extended retention or ship to your SIEM. we'll show retention controls in the Console.
05:43 Priya: access controls and identity — we need SSO, SAML, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC mapped to our groups. can we integrate with Okta?
05:51 Jonah: yes, SSO via SAML and SCIM provisioning for users is supported. RBAC in Console allows role mappings; for Private you can sync to your IdP. we'll provide a sample SAML config and SCIM endpoints.
06:08 Marcus: do you expose a way to redact or mask inputs so PHI or PII doesn't leave Blueleaf?
06:14 Lina: we have built-in pre-processing hooks for token redaction and a streaming redaction filter; it's more mature in Private/Dedicated but available in hosted with config. also caching/prefix caching can be disabled to avoid sensitive KV cache retention.
06:30 Olivia: for encryption keys, can you confirm you support AWS KMS in eu-west-1 and that keys never replicate to us-east-1?
06:38 Jonah: yes for BYOK we support AWS KMS in your account and we don't copy your CMKs. keys remain in your account/region. again, Private eliminates the control-plane copy concerns.
06:50 Priya: is there an attestation or pen test report?
06:54 Samira: we have the SOC2 Type II latest report and a penetration test summary. we'll not share full pentest raw data but can provide executive summaries and remediation status.
07:05 David: operational question — if we want to launch EU-only pilot with 1k qps, how do capacity and latency look?
07:12 Jonah: that's primarily infra sizing — Dedicated GPU pools in eu-west-1 can be provisioned; we'll run a sizing workshop and propose a Dedicated pool. Pilot benchmarks we can run from your infra; we'll coordinate.
07:26 Olivia: ok legal specifics — we need DPA with SCCs and a list of sub-processors that are limited to EU. Priya will follow up with redlines.
07:35 Priya: also need a clause that requires notification of any new sub-processor at least 30 days prior and an option to object.
07:41 Samira: acceptable, we'll include notification commitments.
07:45 Marcus: small nit — for telemetry and metrics, does Redwood ever send payload data to external analytics?
07:50 Lina: by default we collect usage metrics and anonymized latencies, not raw prompt content. we can turn off or route telemetry through your logging in enterprise plans.
08:01 Olivia: what about key rotation and key compromise scenarios — what is the playbook?
08:06 Jonah: for BYOK we rely on your KMS rotation policies; for hosted keys we have rotation processes and can rotate on schedule or in case of compromise; if key compromise happens we coordinate immediate revocation and re-encryption. documented incident response steps are included.
08:22 Samira: i want to call out cross-border processing definitions — we consider any processing where compute or storage is outside EU as cross border. so for EU-only requirement you need Dedicated in-region or Private.
08:36 David: ok, can you make the difference between "region pinning" and "data residency" explicit in the doc? engineers often conflate them.
08:43 Jonah: yes, region pinning is routing for runtime requests; data residency covers where persistent storage, backups, logs live. some setups have pinned runtime but backups replicated elsewhere — we'll make that explicit.
08:58 Priya: do you support contractual restrictions on sub-processors being only in EU?
09:03 Samira: on some enterprise plans yes, we can restrict or remove certain non-EU sub-processors, but some cloud infra providers may still be outside EU for support — we'll enumerate and propose mitigations.
09:18 Olivia: competence question — are there customers in EU finance using Private?
09:22 Samira: yes, a couple of banking customers run Private with their VPC and KMS integrations. we can provide references under NDA.
09:30 Marcus: what about incident logging and forensic data retention for regulatory audit?
09:34 Lina: we can export immutable audit logs to your SIEM (in-region) and set retention/immutability policies. for Private you control the retention entirely.
09:46 Priya: on SCCs — do you add any supplementary measures? how do you handle law enforcement requests?
09:53 Jonah: we follow a transparency principle — we notify customers unless prohibited by law. our DPA also outlines lawful access handling. supplementary measures for transfers are documented; for high-risk customers we recommend Private deployment.
10:09 Olivia: from a timeline perspective, we want pilot in EU only by end of Q4. what's realistic?
10:15 Jonah: if we go Dedicated we can provision capacity in 4-6 weeks after contract; Private depends on your infra timelines but commonly 6-10 weeks. we'll prioritize.
10:26 Samira: next steps recap: we'll send SOC2/ISO and sub-processor list, Jonah will send runbook and region pinning configs, legal team will get DPA and SCCs, Blueleaf to review and propose any redlines.
10:42 Priya: please include an explicit clause about deletion and proof of deletion for backups.
10:47 Samira: noted, we'll include deletion flows and proof-of-delete options (snapshots and deletion confirmation).
10:52 Olivia: thanks all, that was helpful, we'll regroup after docs.
10:56 Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and proposed dates.
